title: Subnet News — October 16, 2026
summary: Null Consensus opens an optional larger competition format, while SN25 UR announces mainnet and a Network Capacity Reserve. SN95 Actual publishes DGX Station inference measurements, SN4 Targon highlights its revenue dashboard, and SN91 Cascade reports a paper-trading result. Also: SN86 re-registration, SN102 ConnitoAI’s finalized coldkey swap, miner rule changes, unresolved incidents and the latest public Shizzy video.

updates.headline: SN3 Teutonic tightens specialist improvement requirements
updates.summary: Primary SN3 Teutonic code now requires specialist own-source improvement to meet the domain threshold, with greater metric-display precision. This changes the qualification signal, rather than treating aggregate performance as sufficient. Community benchmark/threshold chatter was also collected, but its numerical improvements and hardware guidance are not promoted to an official independently verified result.

sources.label: SN3 Teutonic primary specialist threshold change
SN3 Teutonic primary metric precision change

updates.ratingReason: An explicit qualification rule changes what models must demonstrate.

updates.headline: SN4 Targon highlights revenue visibility and enterprise booking
updates.summary: Openτensor’s October 16 Novelty Search announcement describes SN4 Targon’s new GPU capacity being booked within a day, often on year-long enterprise contracts, and points to its public revenue dashboard. The dashboard labels its measure combined platform revenue over the last 30 days. This makes customer activity more visible, but the numeric chart did not render in our public page extraction, so the roughly $583,000 circulated by commentators is not presented as an independently verified current total. Bookings and revenue are attributed claims, not net profit or a completed token buyback. The discussion also separates available cloud products from roadmap services.

sources.label: Openτensor original SN4 Targon episode announcement

updates.ratingReason: A public commercial reporting surface and concrete enterprise-demand claims matter, with chart and financial verification limits explicit.

updates.headline: SN9 IOTA highlights upload constraints amid P2P issues
updates.summary: The October 16 digest attributes a warning that sub-30 Mbit/s upload is not viable to SN9 IOTA’s owner after a miner reported missed weight-upload windows. Primary v4.13.7 release code is available, but a release alone does not establish resolution of every peer-reachability failure. This makes network throughput an operating constraint, not only a GPU specification.
updates.ratingReason: A specific attributed network requirement and active availability problem are useful to miners.

updates.headline: SN10 Pareton adjusts Kimi evaluation while a pause is reported
updates.summary: SN10 Pareton’s primary changes run Kimi K3 at concurrency 32 with eight prompts per tier and allow campaign-specific baseline drift ceilings. The October 16 digest reports a temporary evaluation pause tied to costly and unreliable 8×B300 instances, with a later round expected. This is a changed evaluation setup and attributed availability issue, not a verified restart time. A possible future burn reduction is not treated as already executed.

sources.label: SN10 Pareton primary Kimi evaluation change

updates.ratingReason: Concrete evaluation changes and a reported pause affect miner participation.

updates.headline: SN14 Cacheon reports a faster baseline and updates speculative auditing
updates.summary: The October 16 digest attributes a Qwen3.8-27B baseline upgrade using native speculative decoding and FP8 KV caching to SN14 Cacheon, reporting 57 output tokens/second and a 72% improvement. Those measurements remain attributed. Primary changes audit recurrent MTP state and hybrid prefix keys and allow sealed decode budgets for speculative arenas. Baseline shifts affect the bar miners must beat; this is not an independently reproduced general-speed gain or proof that every validator adopted the update.

sources.label: SN14 Cacheon primary sealed decode-budget change

updates.ratingReason: A changed reference baseline and primary evaluator work materially affect competition conditions.

updates.headline: SN19 Blockmachine reports its sixth buyback
updates.summary: The October 16 digest attributes a $7,475.77 sixth buyback/burn to SN19 Blockmachine, described as 89% above September. Its ambition to offset all miner emissions remains a goal, not an already achieved full offset. The transaction and accounting period were not independently decoded, so this remains an attributed commercial update rather than an audited burn total.
updates.ratingReason: A specific reported buyback milestone is relevant while execution and full-offset claims remain bounded.

updates.headline: SN21 ADTAO adjusts scoring when efficiency cannot be measured
updates.summary: Primary SN21 ADTAO code scores entries without measurable efficiency on cost and conversions. This makes the fallback evaluation basis explicit rather than treating missing efficiency as a valid measured value. It is an implemented scoring change, not independently verified advertiser ROI or validator-wide adoption.
updates.ratingReason: A specific primary fallback rule improves interpretation of miner scores.

updates.headline: SN25 UR announces mainnet and a Network Capacity Reserve
updates.summary: SN25 UR’s October 16 announcement says its validator is active, setting weights and verifying traffic, with permissionless participation. Its existing 100,000-plus network providers are being transitioned—not 100,000 registered miners independently counted today. The October 15 reserve document explains that excess miner emissions become working capital to commission useful connectivity ahead of operator demand, rather than all being distributed immediately. The reserve is described as a separate multisig, with payments conditional on verified commitments and disclosed transfers. This connects a privacy-network service to Bittensor incentives. The document distinguishes current routing verification from stronger geographic/traffic verification that proposed programs would require; future reserve payouts and customer growth are not already proven. At the same finalized head, SN25 UR has 256 registered UIDs under Yuma; this is a direct check against interpreting the provider-transition headline as 100,000 on-chain UIDs.
updates.ratingReason: An official mainnet announcement plus primary operating design advances a real network beyond a scheduled launch, while rollout counts remain bounded.

Code availability is verified; successful paid production requests and provider-wide rollout were not exercised, and route documentation is not a universal confidential-compute guarantee.

sources.label: SN28 SayGM primary SN53 Engy video-route implementation

updates.headline: SN37 Aurelius adds runtime-479 miner compatibility
updates.summary: SN37 Aurelius’ primary miner change explicitly supports the reviewed mainnet runtime 479. The October 16 digest reports mining live and a separate WT balance-transfer delay under investigation. Runtime compatibility is verified code; fleet activation, individual balances and complete recovery were not independently tested.
updates.ratingReason: A concrete compatibility change and attributed activation/incident update affect participation.

updates.headline: SN41 Almanac adds recovery for transient forecasting failures
updates.summary: SN41 Almanac’s merged PR 58 adds retries, logging, timeouts and stale-weight fallback, with weights version 4. The primary change describes fallback for up to six hours when scoring data cannot be gathered. A digest attributes two zero-weight forecasting epochs to transient API failures. The patch is a concrete resilience change; the reported 6–8% incentive impact and fleet-wide adoption were not independently reconstructed. Validators need the updated deployment rather than assuming a merge repairs an already running instance.
updates.ratingReason: A primary fix directly targets an availability failure affecting forecasting weights.

updates.headline: SN44 Score reports restored run data; another detector is planned
updates.summary: The October 16 digest attributes a fixed read error and restored run JSON to SN44 Score. Fallen-person detection is described as expected next, not already verified live. Yesterday’s scoring/enforcement complaints are not automatically resolved, and the new box-overlay social clip was not fully reviewed as a release demonstration.
updates.ratingReason: A bounded data-access repair is kept separate from future detection support and unresolved scoring.

updates.summary: The October 16 SN54 Yanez digest attributes delayed Phase 4 Cycle 5 UAV rewards to scoring roughly two million submissions, including manual screen-replay reviews. Phase 5 execution is now expected by October 19, without an additional delay bonus. This revises timing rather than proving rewards have been finalized or paid. updates.headline: SN62 Ridges explains dynamic upload prices
updates.summary: SN62 Ridges’ October 15 post and upload-pricing guide specify default submission pricing with a $5 floor, approximately 15% increase per purchased upload, and a 30-minute half-life between purchases. Unused alpha can carry forward, with a top-up flow when the price changes during submission. This changes the cost and timing of joining coding competitions; it is not a fixed $5 fee or a guarantee that an upload will earn rewards.
updates.ratingReason: Concrete published admission economics affect participants directly.

updates.headline: SN64 Chutes details its Parallax training-cost example
updates.summary: SN64 Chutes’ October 15 post describes an 8B pretraining run across rented RTX 5090s over the internet:574 billion tokens in 52 hours, around $6,500 and $11.27 per billion tokens. Four CPU VMs are described as syncers. This is a concrete team-reported training example; retail-price comparisons with a differently sized/reference run are estimates rather than like-for-like independent benchmarking. A new post about a run is not automatically the run’s completion date.

sources.label: SN64 Chutes original Parallax cost/setup explanation

updates.summary: SN81 Reliquary’s primary environment release appends 1,893 competitive-code problems for supervised fine-tuning. Its release notes keep previous training indices and evaluation/qualification sets unchanged and describe decontamination against those held-out sources. This expands training material without claiming a new benchmark score; data-policy implementation is not an independent contamination audit.
updates.ratingReason: A specific training-data release is substantive and its evaluation boundary is documented.

updates.headline: SN86 was removed and re-registered; sale terms are unverified
updates.summary: Late-found direct chain evidence places NetworkRemoved at block 9,289,316 on October 15 at 14:26:48 UTC, in extrinsic 18, alongside a new registration queue entry. NetworkAdded follows at block 9,289,319 at 14:27:24 UTC; the registration-height storage and new owner key match. The queued lock is 493.992245801 TAO, a protocol registration lock—not a negotiated purchase price. The screener now labels the slot OnSale, but that label does not identify a buyer or prove a sale. These events precede yesterday’s stated cutoff by minutes but occurred after its recorded node head, so they are explicitly backfilled today. The identity of any new operating team remains unconfirmed.

sources.label: SN86 decoded removal and queue block

updates.ratingReason: Decoded events and before/after storage establish a real slot replacement rather than inferring a sale from price or a name.

This is published operator policy, not evidence every older node was removed today or that every advertised hardware configuration has been independently validated.

updates.headline: SN95 Actual publishes DGX Station inference measurements
updates.summary: SN95 Actual’s October 15 case study introduces its e engine on NVIDIA DGX Station with Nemotron 3.5 Super VL. It reports preliminary decode measurements of 455 tokens/second for one stream and over 8,000 across 128 streams, with 0.58-second first-token latency for a fresh 8K-token prompt. The stated setup uses FP8 weights and MTP. This is a concrete effort to serve department-scale agent workloads on owned hardware. These are team measurements, not an independently reproduced comparison; a hosted model and a local open model are not interchangeable quality/cost benchmarks. The confidential relay claim concerns the described relay architecture, not proof of privacy on every endpoint.

ecosystem.headline: Null Consensus offers larger competitions—with a single weight-setting validator
ecosystem.summary: Openτensor’s October 15 release announcement and primary documentation describe an owner-selected alternative to Yuma. Null permits capacity up to floor(2,500/mechanism count), versus floor(256/mechanism count) under Yuma; switching does not automatically expand a subnet. The highest unrounded-stake registered UID becomes the sole validator permitted to submit weights, and consensus/bond calculations are skipped. That creates room for bigger competitions and precise integer reward ratios, while concentrating weight-setting authority. Yuma remains the default and root cannot select Null. Optional proof-of-work registration is independently available for Null or Yuma: a direct zero-tip submission needs no registration burn, initial collateral purchase or transaction fee, but still requires computational work and obeys admission rules. Const’s October 15 quote welcomes the added scale and freedom; that is commentary, not evidence every subnet has switched. Direct finalized storage at block 9,296,035 confirms SN120 Affine already using Null with capacity 1,000 and PoW enabled; SN25 UR and SN128 byteleap.ai remain Yuma with capacity 256. The release index separately labels a 16,000-capacity Null version upcoming, conflicting with the guide/post’s 2,500 description. We do not assume that larger version is active; exact per-subnet configuration takes precedence.

sources.label: Primary Null configuration and registration documentation
Primary release index; larger Null version labelled upcoming

ecosystem.ratingReason: A primary protocol release materially changes competition capacity, admission options and trust assumptions across Bittensor.

ecosystem.headline: eTAO emission-weight code is published; finalized runtime remains 479
ecosystem.summary: The primary repository contains spec-480 eTAO per-subnet emission-weight work. Our finalized archive-node check at block 9,296,035 still reports runtime 479. Published implementation and active-chain deployment are separate facts: this report does not call spec 480 live or assume its new controls are already available. The current immunity and registration-cost decay parameters match yesterday’s checked values. This matters because subnet teams should follow actual activation gates, not treat every merged or branch commit as a mainnet upgrade.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Substantial protocol implementation is relevant, with the observed activation boundary retained.
